title: Coral and the Summit
premise: Blacklisted mountain guide Hazel Nystrom has spent two decades running from the avalanche that killed her climbing partner, measuring her life in safe miles. When dying prospector Eben Voss trades her a map to a forbidden glacial source in exchange for a promise to deliver it to the valley his family was exiled from, she finds herself saddled with his estranged grandson, Tomas, who wants the map destroyed and his grandfather's sins buried with him. Racing the calving season up the Serpent River, Hazel and Tomas uncover that the source sits on land her own government drowned in scandal — and that her blacklist was bought by the same company now racing to seal the valley forever. In the end, Hazel must choose between the loyalty that kept her alive and the truth that will ruin her: she exposes the cover-up at the summit, loses her last chance at reinstatement, and gains something rarer — a life measured in years, with Tomas, in the valley Voss died to give back.
about_author: Xanthe Iversen is a former expedition cook who turned twenty seasons of base-camp gossip and glacier lore into fiction. She writes from a converted fishing cabin on the Norwegian coast, where the weather does her editing for her.

chapters.title: The Weight of Miles
chapters.summary: Hazel Nystrom guides a routine trek through the Greywater Range, counting switchbacks instead of birthdays. A client's careless question about her blacklist stings; her quiet ritual of leaving a cairn for her dead partner closes the chapter. POV: Hazel. Beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: In a roadside saloon, dying prospector Eben Voss recognizes Hazel from her banned days and offers a hand-drawn map of the Serpent River's forbidden source — if she swears to carry it to the Voss family's exiled valley. She refuses, then watches him collapse. POV: Hazel. Beat: guilt arriving before consent.

chapters.title: The Grandson Who Says Burn It
chapters.summary: At Voss's deathbed, his grandson Tomas arrives furious, insisting the map is a liar's fantasy that disgraced the family. Voss dies mid-sentence, leaving Hazel bound by a promise and Tomas by a grudge. POV: Tomas. Beat: grief weaponized into opposition.

chapters.title: Two Debts, One River
chapters.summary: Hazel decides to honor the promise alone; Tomas follows to intercept her, and a flash flood forces them to camp together. They strike a bitter bargain: he comes along, and if the valley proves real, they decide the map's fate together. POV: Hazel. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Where the River Learns Its Name
chapters.summary: Following the Serpent upstream through canyon country, Hazel teaches Tomas river-reading; he teaches her the family stories Voss never told. A ranger checkpoint nearly exposes her banned status, and Tomas lies for her — surprising them both. POV: Tomas. Beat: trust's first thin ice.

chapters.title: The Company's Shadow
chapters.summary: In a supply town, Hazel discovers survey crews from Halvard Extraction staking the upper Serpent — the same firm whose name appears on her old blacklist paperwork. She photographs the crews; a spotter photographs her. POV: Hazel. Beat: the past isn't past, it's employed.

chapters.title: What Voss Actually Found
chapters.summary: Decoding the map's margins, Tomas realizes his grandfather didn't find gold — he found evidence the valley's flooding decades ago was engineered to hide contamination, with Voss paid to stay silent. His loyalty to the family name cracks. POV: Tomas. Beat: truth as betrayal's twin.

chapters.title: The Cold Camp
chapters.summary: A storm strands them above treeline for three days. In the dark, Hazel tells the truth about the avalanche — she cut the rope to save herself, and the blacklist was the company's price for silence. Tomas doesn't flinch. POV: Hazel. Beat: confession as first intimacy.

chapters.title: Spotters on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Halvard's men shadow the route, having traced Voss's map from his deathbed visitor log. A tense game of cat-and-mouse through scree fields ends with their supplies stolen and a warning: turn back or be buried. POV: Tomas. Beat: the stakes turn lethal.

chapters.title: The Shortcut That Isn't
chapters.summary: Losing days, Hazel proposes the banned Kestrel Traverse — the route from her old life. Tomas sees the route is a wound she's avoiding, and pushes her to face it. They cross; she doesn't shake. POV: Hazel. Beat: reclaiming the miles she feared.

chapters.title: A Valley That Answers
chapters.summary: The river narrows into a gorge that matches the map exactly — the valley is real. But so are fresh dynamite crates at its mouth. Halvard is sealing the source before calving season, and the calendar is against them. POV: Tomas. Beat: hope with a timer on it.

chapters.title: The Man in the Crate Road
chapters.summary: They ambush a Halvard surveyor, Renn, who reveals the company's plan: collapse the source cavern, blame it on calving, and erase the contamination evidence forever. He also recognizes Hazel — and hesitates, because she once saved his brother on a mountain. POV: Renn (guest) shifting to Hazel. Beat: an enemy with a conscience.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tomas argues to take Renn's stolen detonator plans to the press from the last signal town — a two-day detour that means missing the calving window. Hazel refuses; the promise comes first. They fight, and he walks. POV: Tomas. Beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: Alone Upstream
chapters.summary: Hazel pushes solo through the gorge, faster but brittle, haunted by how the last time she climbed alone someone died. Renn reappears, off the clock, offering to guide her through Halvard's blast perimeter — for nothing. POV: Hazel. Beat: grace from an unexpected quarter.

chapters.title: What Tomas Carried
chapters.summary: Tomas, halfway to the signal town, reads Voss's final letter — tucked in his pack since chapter 3 — and learns his grandfather's silence bought the family's safety, not their shame. He turns back. POV: Tomas. Beat: loyalty re-forged by truth, not instead of it.

chapters.title: The Perimeter
chapters.summary: Hazel and Renn slip the blast perimeter at night, but a floodlamp sweep pins them; Renn surrenders himself as a decoy so she can run the icefall. His last words: 'My brother would want the math to come out even.' POV: Hazel. Beat: sacrifice as repayment.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Hazel reaches the glacial source: a cathedral of blue ice lacing a poisoned spring, Voss's evidence cache intact in a steel drum — water samples, ledgers, photographs of the flooding crews. She hears the calving season's first deep cracks. POV: Hazel. Beat: awe and deadline in one breath.

chapters.title: Tomas on the Ice
chapters.summary: Tomas arrives half-frozen across the icefall, having evaded the search teams. They open the drum together and find the final document: Voss's signed confession naming the Halvard executive who blacklisted Hazel to bury her testimony. POV: Tomas. Beat: the map's true inheritance.

chapters.title: The Calving
chapters.summary: The glacier's face lets go. In a white roar, Hazel and Tomas race the collapse along the icefall as the source cavern begins to seal — Halvard's premature charges, triggered by the calving, are collapsing the evidence chamber. They dig the drum free as the world comes down. POV: Hazel. Beat: climax — nature, greed, and promise converging.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Summit
chapters.summary: Above the valley rim, with the drum in hand, Hazel faces her choice: trade Voss's evidence for reinstatement and her name back, or publish it and stay blacklisted forever. Tomas tells her he'll stand by either. She chooses truth. POV: Hazel. Beat: love against duty, resolved.

chapters.title: The Valley Voss Gave Back
chapters.summary: The evidence breaks in the press; Halvard's executives fall, Renn testifies, and the exiled Voss descendants — Tomas's kin — are granted access to the valley. Hazel's blacklist is exposed as retaliation, but the licensing boards stall; her name is cleared in the papers, not yet on the permit. POV: Tomas. Beat: justice, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: Measured in Years
chapters.summary: One year later, Hazel leads her first trek — unlicensed, small, honest — into the reopened valley, where a cairn for Eben Voss stands beside the one for her partner, finally at peace. She plants a new cairn with no name on it: the mile she no longer needs to count. POV: Hazel. Beat: resolution — a life measured in years, together.
